card.title: The Emotional Center
card.instruction: Carry yourself as the emotional center of the room, letting your mood determine what deserves attention and how seriously it should be treated.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before your good news, I need everyone to understand my afternoon.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Wonderful. Hold that feeling while I finish the parking story.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're waiting on a video call for us to toast.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put me on first. They need the parking story, or my face will look like a comment on your promotion.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 puts A's afternoon before B's news, A3 pauses the promotion feeling for parking, and A5 requires the wider toast audience to understand A's face first.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's promotion informs A3's hold-that-feeling instruction; B4's waiting video group becomes A5's demand for first airtime.

relationship.evidence: B2 has genuine good news and B4 identifies people already waiting to celebrate it.

heightening.evidence: A5 uses B4's larger audience to expand the emotional briefing rather than yield the floor.

specificity.evidence: A1-B2 establish competing personal news and B4 supplies the live toast context.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's face-as-comment explanation connects the parking story to B4's visible call audience.
